finding.title: Inject analyticsServiceProvider into MarkLiveCompletionUseCase so tutor_live_mark_blocked actually fires
finding.why: grep -rn 'MarkLiveCompletionUseCase<' across lib/ shows text_display_screen.dart:669 is the ONLY production construction site in the app, and it omits the optional `analytics:` argument, so `_analytics` stays null and the null-aware `_analytics?.logEvent(...)` silently no-ops. The use case's own comment says this telemetry exists so 'tutor boundary violations are visible in dashboards' (W7.11) — the permission guard itself still works (exception thrown, dialog shown), but that dashboard signal never fires anywhere in production, so ops has zero visibility into how often the tutor write-boundary is hit.
finding.recommendation: Pass analytics: ref.read(analyticsServiceProvider) at the construction site — the provider already exists and is used the same way by sibling tutoring providers (tutor_grant_providers.dart).
acceptance_criteria: a widget/unit test overrides analyticsServiceProvider with a fake, drives a tutor-session mark-complete attempt, and asserts logEvent(LogEvents.tutor.liveMarkBlocked) was called exactly once

finding.title: Rewrite tests that don't actually exercise the repository/provider they claim to test

evidence.quote: skip: 'Bundled JSON removed — content now fetched from cloud storage',

finding.why: content_repository_impl_test.dart's 'in-memory operations' group re-implements ContentRepositoryImpl's filter/search logic with local .where() calls instead of calling filterByLevel/search/getContentByRef — a regression in the real nikud-stripping cache or level-matching would not be caught here. Its 'empty search returns empty list' test is a pure tautology that doesn't reference the repository at all. Its entire 'JSON parsing contract' group is skipped with a now-false premise (ContentRepositoryImpl.getContentForCurriculum still loads rootBundle.loadString('assets/content/hierarchy/$key.json'), and 14 such files exist) and even unskipped would fail immediately since its own File('assets/content/$filename') omits the 'hierarchy/' path segment. Separately, content_tile_search_providers_test.dart's 'P2. empty query' test allocates a ProviderContainer and disposes it but never calls container.read(...) — its assertion only exercises the hand-written fake repository directly, not contentSearchProvider as the test name claims. The sibling file content_repository_impl_logic_test.dart (also in this batch) shows the correct pattern — a fake subclass that only stubs asset loading and calls the real repository methods — so real coverage exists elsewhere, but these weaker duplicates sit alongside it giving false confidence.
finding.recommendation: Delete the 'in-memory operations' and skipped 'JSON parsing contract' groups from content_repository_impl_test.dart (superseded by content_repository_impl_logic_test.dart); add one small always-on smoke test that loads and parses every assets/content/hierarchy/*.json file; fix the P2 test to call container.read(contentSearchProvider(...).future) with an empty query.
acceptance_criteria: mutating ContentRepositoryImpl.search's nikud-stripping or filterByLevel's level-matching logic causes a red test in this suite after the rewrite
dart test shows 0 permanently-skipped groups in content_repository_impl_test.dart, or the skip reason is corrected and carries a Linear id

finding.title: Type the catch clauses in content_browsing instead of bare catch(e)
finding.why: None of these restrict the caught type, so each also catches Error subtypes (a TypeError from a bad cast, a StateError from a logic bug) and handles them as an ordinary recoverable failure. The sharpest case is cloud_content_service.dart:317 (currently dead per the separate dead-code finding, but worth fixing if kept): if gzip.decode throws for a reason other than 'not gzipped' (e.g. a truncated download), the function returns the still-compressed bytes as valid data, turning a clear decompression failure into a confusing downstream JSON-parse error. text_display_screen.dart:755's bare catch(e, st) around _handleComplete will show 'Could not save' for a genuine programming bug exactly the same way it shows it for an expected write failure.
finding.recommendation: Narrow each to on FormatException/on Exception catch as appropriate; for the gzip fallback specifically, check the gzip magic number (0x1f 0x8b) instead of try/catch.
acceptance_criteria: a grep-based Rule-0 check for '} catch (' without a preceding 'on ' returns zero hits in these 4 files (or dart run custom_lint once its analyzer-9.0 incompatibility, already baselined, is fixed)

finding.title: Add keepAlive justification comments to live content_browsing providers
finding.why: SM-6 requires an inline justification beside every keepAlive: true so a reviewer can tell a deliberate cache-lifetime decision from a copy-pasted default. None of these three explain why losing the cached value on last-listener-disappear would be wrong — contrast with contentRepositoryProvider 3 lines above curriculumHeNames in the same file, which does explain it ('rebuilding this provider would discard cached data').
finding.recommendation: Add a one-line '// keepAlive: <reason>' per the pattern already used in sync_orchestrator_providers.dart, e.g. for FontSizeNotifier/ShowNikud: 'font-size/nikud toggles must survive navigating away from the reader and back.'
acceptance_criteria: the [Pending] audit grep requiring a justification comment beside keepAlive: true (coding-standards.md SM-6) finds a comment within 2 lines of each @Riverpod(keepAlive: true) in this feature
